---
title: "check-orphaned-images.yml"
---

Report tracked image files that no tracked source file references.
A figure that stops being used, because its page was rewritten or a
regenerated copy was committed under a new name, stays in the repository
indefinitely, since a render never notices a file it was not asked to read.

## What counts as a use

An image is used when its **file name** appears in any tracked file whose
extension is in `source-extensions`: a Markdown image, a YAML key such as
`favicon:`, a CSS `url()`, a Lua string, an HTML `src`.
Names are compared case-insensitively and after URL-decoding, so
`my%20fig.png` matches `my fig.png`.
Only tracked images are examined, so render output and untracked scratch files
are never reported.

Matching the file name rather than a resolved path is deliberate, since
resolving every relative, root-relative, YAML, Lua, and CSS reference is what a
render does.
It has two costs:

- two images that share a file name in different directories are both counted
  as used when either one is;
- an image named only by a computed string, such as
  `paste0("fig", i, ".png")`, reads as unused and needs `paths-ignore`.

The default `source-extensions` leave out `.R` and `.py`, since a script that
*writes* a figure names it too, which would hide the figure no page shows.
Add them when a script, rather than a page, is what uses a figure.

## Warn-only by default

An unused file breaks nothing, and a name search cannot see every way a file
can be used, so findings are warnings unless `fail: true`.
Set `added-only: true` to report only the images a pull request adds, so a
first run over years of accumulated figures does not bury the one a pull
request just added.
With `added-only`, events other than a pull request skip the check rather than
examine the whole tree.

## Inputs

| Input | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `paths` | string | `'.'` | Space-separated git pathspecs to look for images in (recursive). |
| `extensions` | string | `'.png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .svg, .webp, .avif'` | Image file extensions to examine. |
| `source-extensions` | string | `'.qmd, .md, .Rmd, .ipynb, .yml, .yaml, .scss, .css, .lua, .html, .tex, .bib'` | Extensions of the tracked files searched for references. |
| `paths-ignore` | string | `''` | Comma- or newline-separated globs (`*`, `?`, `**`) of images to skip. |
| `added-only` | boolean | `false` | On pull requests, report only images the PR adds; skip other events. |
| `fail` | boolean | `false` | Fail the job on a finding (else warn only). |

The composite action takes `base-ref` in place of `added-only`: set, only
images added since the merge base with that ref are reported, and when the
merge base cannot be computed the check is skipped with a warning rather than
widened to the whole tree.

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
name: Check orphaned images
on:
  push: { branches: [main] }
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:
jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-orphaned-images.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   paths: 'images/'
    #   paths-ignore: 'images/generated/**'
    #   added-only: true
    #   fail: true
```

See `check-orphaned-images.yml` in
[`examples/`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/tree/main/examples)
for the full caller stub.
